subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw make compact, goal-shaped browser reads the default behavior, and what explicit raw/full escape hatch should remain for workflows that need complete page state?
rationale: Current main has caps and an efficient mode, but choosing default model-facing browser semantics changes the browser tool contract and needs owner intent before automation chooses the behavior.

options.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
options.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable, keep explicit full/raw AI/ARIA reads for complete refs, and validate both paths with browser plugin tests and live proof.

options.title: Keep opt-in efficient mode
options.body: Leave current defaults intact and document mode=efficient, maxChars, selector reads, and generic pruning for context-heavy browser workflows.

options.title: Fold into browser roadmap
options.body: Track this under the broader browser field-report work only if maintainers want one umbrella for action diffs, stale refs, viewport reads, and context shaping.

recommendation.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
recommendation.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable, keep explicit full/raw AI/ARIA reads for complete refs, and validate both paths with browser plugin tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the browser plugin product boundary and snapshot contract comes from steipete's early browser snapshot/runtime ownership work.
